If sentiment is positive in the last 3 days and forecast is trending up, reduce forecast by 1–2% for early horizon (1–7 days).  
If sentiment is negative and forecast is trending down, increase forecast by 1–2% for mid horizon (8–15 days).  
If sentiment is neutral and forecast is flat, apply a 0.5–1.5% upward adjustment for late horizon (16–30 days) to capture momentum.  
When sentiment shifts from negative to positive within 5 days, add a 1–3% upward bias to forecast starting from day 6.  
If sentiment is consistently positive over 10+ days, reduce forecast by 0.5–1.5% for all horizons to avoid overconfidence.  
If sentiment is negative and forecast is above true value, subtract 1–2% from forecast for late horizon (16–30 days) to correct overreaction.
